s: An education company is running a web application used by college students around the world. The application runs in an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). A system administrator detected a weekly spike in the number of failed logic attempts. Which overwhelm the application's authentication service. All the failed login attempts originate from about 500 different IP addresses that change each week. A solutions architect must prevent the failed login attempts from overwhelming the authentication service. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
o: Use AWS Firewall Manager to create a security group and security group policy to deny access from the IP addresses.
Create an AWS WAF web ACL with a rate-based rule, and set the rule action to Block. Connect the web ACL to the ALB.
Use AWS Firewall Manager to create a security group and security group policy to allow access only to specific CIDR ranges.
Create an AWS WAF web ACL with an IP set match rule, and set the rule action to Block. Connect the web ACL to the ALB.
e: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) on the Application Load Balancer is the most operationally efficient solution because: l Rate-based rules: Can detect and block IP addresses making excessive failed login attempts, protecting the authentication service from being overwhelmed l Automatic IP blocking: WAF can automatically block IPs exceeding defined request thresholds without manual intervention l Minimal operational overhead: Rules are managed centrally and automatically applied to all traffic before it reaches the application l Handles changing IPs: Rate-based rules work regardless of whether the attacking IPs change weekly, as blocking is dynamic based on behavior This is superior to network-layer solutions (NACLs/security groups) which require manual IP management, or application-level rate limiting which consumes application resources. WAF provides protection at the edge with minimal overhead.

w.y: The attacking IPs change every week, so blocking specific addresses fails. A WAF rate-based rule on the ALB blocks any IP that sends too many requests, with no weekly updates.

o.A: Security groups cannot deny traffic, and the IP list changes every week.
o.B: Correct: WAF rate-based rule on the ALB blocks noisy IPs automatically.
o.C: Allowing only certain CIDR ranges blocks legitimate students worldwide.
o.D: An IP set must be updated every week as the addresses change.
